b678ee7604: Multiplication multiplies the moduli and adds the arguments — geometrically, it scales and rotates. This is exactly what De Moivre's theorem generalizes to powers and roots.

f50106e424: Because angles that differ by a full turn (2π) describe the same point, but raising to the nth power multiplies the angle by n — so n different starting angles, spaced 2π/n apart, all land on the same result.

0a2cf25790: Besides division, z·z̄ = |z|² always gives a real number, which is essential for finding magnitudes, normalizing vectors, and in signal processing for computing power from a complex amplitude.
